heading: INT. HOTEL BELMONT-CRANE - PNEUMATIC TUBE ROOM - NIGHT

units.text: INT. HOTEL BELMONT-CRANE - PNEUMATIC TUBE ROOM - NIGHT
A windowless room behind the front desk.
Brass tubes snake up the walls to every floor, thumping quietly with canisters in transit.
A sorting table.
A single green-shaded lamp.
A black candlestick telephone on a stool.
DETECTIVE ISIDORE QUAYLE, 50s, rumpled overcoat, hat in hand, studies a brass canister.
CONCIERGE THEO LAMBERT, 30s, tailcoat, silver hair too early, stands very straight at the table.
MRS. GLADYS BRANDYWINE, 60s, hotel owner, pearls, black dress, sits on a wooden chair with her handbag in her lap.
Mr. Lambert, how long have you operated the tubes?
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: Eleven years, sir.
units.name: LAMBERT

units.text: And this evening you sent a canister to room 614.
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: At eleven oh two. A message from the front desk.
units.name: LAMBERT

units.text: What was the message?
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: I didn't read it.
units.name: LAMBERT

units.text: He never reads them, Detective.
units.name: MRS. BRANDYWINE

units.text: Madam, I'm asking Mr. Lambert.
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: And I am telling you that he is a professional.
units.name: MRS. BRANDYWINE

units.text: Thank you, Mrs. Brandywine.
units.name: LAMBERT

units.text: Who gave you the message?
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: A guest. A lady in grey.
units.name: LAMBERT

units.text: Gladys.
units.name: MRS. BRANDYWINE

units.text: I beg your pardon?
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: My name is Gladys. I wore grey tonight.
units.name: MRS. BRANDYWINE

units.text: Madam. Are you telling me you wrote the message?
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: I am telling you nothing, Detective. I am correcting Mr. Lambert's description.
units.name: MRS. BRANDYWINE

units.text: Mrs. Brandywine, I never said it was you.
units.name: LAMBERT

units.text: No, Theo. You didn't.
units.name: MRS. BRANDYWINE

units.text: The telephone rings.
Everyone stops.
Quayle lifts the receiver.
Quayle.
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: Detective, I have a call from Room 614.
units.name: OPERATOR

units.text: Put it through.
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: Sir, it's already connected. Sir, I think the line is open.
units.name: OPERATOR

units.text: Is anyone speaking?
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: No sir. I hear a clock.
units.name: OPERATOR

units.text: A clock?
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: Ticking. Very loud.
units.name: OPERATOR

units.text: Quayle holds the receiver away from his ear.
All four hear it faintly, a metronome in the dark: tick, tick, tick.
The grandfather clock in the penthouse hall.
units.name: LAMBERT

units.text: That clock stopped in 1929.
units.name: MRS. BRANDYWINE

units.text: Then who wound it?
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: Neither answers.
A canister thumps in the tube.
A second, a third.
They roll into the sorting tray, one after another.
These aren't mine.
units.name: LAMBERT

units.text: Open them.
units.name: MRS. BRANDYWINE

units.text: Madam!
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: Open them, Detective, or I will.
units.name: MRS. BRANDYWINE

units.text: Quayle snaps the first one open.
Pulls out a slip of cream paper.
Reads it.
His face goes blank.
What does it say?
units.name: LAMBERT

units.text: "He's behind the wall."
units.name: QUAYLE

units.text: Silence.
The tubes thump.
The clock ticks on the telephone.
Mrs. Brandywine stands, smooths her dress.
I told you not to open them.
units.name: MRS. BRANDYWINE

units.text: Sir? Sir? The ticking has stopped.
units.name: OPERATOR

units.text: The lamp flickers, then goes out.
In the dark, the tubes all begin to thump together.
